# v0.24.0 — hermes-lcm-x: catalog identity (BREAKING rename) and compaction fixes

Promotes the runtime bytes qualified in `v0.24.0-rc4` (`9fd8846fc0e8dd4d9c3a58e5cbd5611aef6f711a`). The only source-tree change from that
candidate is this added release-note file. Qualification: RELEASE-READINESS-V1 Phases A, B and C, summarized below.

**BREAKING.** The plugin is renamed `hermes-lcm` → `hermes-lcm-x` and the context engine `lcm` →
`lcm-x`, so LCM-X can enter the Hermes plugin catalog under its own identity (#471). An in-place
update with an unchanged config stops loading LCM-X; follow the migration steps below before
restarting Hermes. The store (`lcm.db`), the `lcm:` config block, `LCM_*` environment variables,
the 15 `lcm_*` tools, `/lcm` and the "LCM plugin loaded" log line are unchanged. No default and no
privacy posture changed.

## RC qualification

`RELEASE-READINESS-V1` ran against the rc4 commit `9fd8846fc0e8dd4d9c3a58e5cbd5611aef6f711a`.

- [Phase A](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.24.0/PHASE-A-RECEIPT.md): 30/30 tool-matrix rows, all 15 registered tools in both postures, 4/4 privacy and misconfiguration batteries, coverage complete, on Hermes 37aad38c.
- [Phase B](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.24.0/PHASE-B-RECEIPT.md): cross-model sweeps of the v0.23.3 → rc4 diff and the rc3 → rc4 delta
  (gpt-6-astra) found no P0, P1, P2 or P3. Hands-on: upgrade v0.23.3 → rc4 → v0.23.3 and rc3 → rc4 (earlier proofs honoured, 0 duplicates on the rc3 path), the read-only eva SQL counter with positive and negative controls, the real-PluginManager matrix on Hermes 37aad38c, 639823919c, v2026.9.24 and upstream main e5131dc with no skipped test, the #488 and #499 measurements quoted below, and the default-config live-shape regression (8/8 cells: 160 stored rows, 0 duplicates, 0 conflicts, rotation sessions = compactions + 1).
- [Phase C](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.24.0/PHASE-C-RECEIPT.md): live Hermes ACP soaks, 44 turns each (40 material + 4 probes) on eva's provider, six cells: C1 native OFF in-place and C2 native OFF rotation on `37aad38c` (5 committed compactions each; same-session restart re-bind and rotation carry PASS), C3 native OFF and C4 native ON on `639823919c` (4 and 5 committed; C4 native adoptions 5/5), C5 native ON on Hermes `v2026.9.24` (8 native adoptions committed; 4 attempts aborted safely, no loss), C6 native OFF in-place on `37aad38c` with leading-space and trailing-newline prompts (6 committed; whitespace preserved 6/6). Every cell: 88/88 transcript rows stored, 0 missing, 0 replayed rows on the independent SQL counter (positive control: 666 on the rc3 failure), 0 conflicts, probes 3/3 exact. Instrument note: the mandated exactly-once hash bar reported FAIL on C3/C4 because the model produced 23 and 25 byte-identical replies on that host and a one-to-one content matcher cannot pair identical items; the receipt records the lane's FAIL verdict, the multiset re-score of all six cells (PASS 6/6, with a positive control that still fails the rc3 replay case) and the release controller's adjudication.


## Changes since v0.24.0-rc3 (#494, #495, #482, #487)

rc3 failed its live soak: in a live Hermes ACP session, compactions committed, but the next turn stored
copies of the compacted rows and later compactions were refused (666 duplicate rows in 36 turns). rc4
fixes that path and three more duplicate or skip paths found while qualifying the fix. With default LCM settings
the same ACP path was worse on rc3: in a real-host harness (80 turns), every compaction after the first was refused, and from turn 55
new turns were no longer stored in `lcm.db` because the host could not fit the context. rc4 stores all 80 turns with no duplicates.

- **Host rewrites of a stored prompt (#494).** Hermes' ACP adapter hands the raw prompt to the turn, and at
  turn end rewrites the same message to its trimmed form. LCM-X had already stored the raw form, so its
  exact matchers no longer recognized the row. LCM-X now notices when the host changes the edge whitespace
  of a user message it stored in the same process, and records the host's form as an extra identity for
  that row, in a metadata row keyed by its store id. The stored message, its search index and its order are
  never modified. Whitespace tolerance applies only at positions a compaction proof binds. The durable
  proof is now written as version 3, and rc3's version 2 proofs are still read.
- **Rotation (#495). Correction to rc3:** the rc3 notes said rotation runs stored no duplicate rows. That
  held only for the test configuration. With realistic turn sizes, a rotated child session could not
  publish the parent's carried rows. Hermes then took the unchanged result as progress, rotated again
  without a proof, and the new child stored the whole context again (1,802 duplicate rows and 41 sessions
  in an 80-turn default-config run on rc3). A rotation child that consumed a compaction proof now publishes
  the parent's carried rows through durable carry ranges; raw rows stay owned by the parent. A result that
  differs only in host-private fields returns the host's own list, so Hermes takes its no-progress path.
  Without a system message, the summary now arrives merged into the oldest kept user turn, exactly as
  Hermes would merge it, so the child's saved transcript never outgrows it. When such a row is compacted
  later, the summarizer sees only the user's text, not the summary again. rc4 on that run: 160 rows, 0 duplicates, 6 sessions.
- **Native recovery (#482, #487; `LCM_NATIVE_RECOVERY=true`, off by default).** On a host that exposes its
  private compaction markers, native recovery compresses only the rows before LCM-X's protected tail and
  re-attaches the tail unchanged, so Hermes' pruning can no longer rewrite it and get the summary rejected
  (#482); without those markers it keeps the previous full-transcript path. Host adoption of a native summary now records a
  compaction proof like LCM-X's own compactions, so the adopted list is not stored again (#487; about 100
  duplicate rows per adoption before). Real-host matrix: 36 cells on three Hermes revisions, no lost rows,
  no stored summary rows.

## Changes since v0.24.0-rc2 (#483, #484, #486)

Hermes in-place compaction (`compression.in_place`, on by default) commits a compaction by calling the
context engine's session-end hook with the pre-compaction list, then restarting the same session id. Up to
rc2, LCM-X treated that call as a real session end: it reset the published frontier to 0, so every later
compaction in that session was refused, and it re-ingested the pre-compaction list (about 50 duplicate rows
per turn on a live profile) (#483).

- Each `compress()` call records a proof of the exact message identities it received and returned, bound to
  its session and conversation. A session end whose messages equal that input is a compaction commit: it
  keeps the session's own frontier and does not re-ingest, and the following same-id start keeps the ingest
  position. A session sharing a conversation never inherits another session's frontier.
- The proof is written to `lcm.db` as one metadata row per compacted session (no schema change), so a
  restart or a rotation resumes at the proven position. A crash between a rotation's parent end and child
  start is not covered (#489).
- No replay match relies on a lossy-by-design stored form (password redaction), and a summary merged into
  a user turn is skipped only when it matches one of the session's own stored summaries exactly (#486).

## Changes since v0.24.0-rc1 (#477, #478)

- The `identity_migration` notice leads with stop Hermes → edit `config.yaml` → start Hermes, and names the
  live-edit fallback when the `lcm` alias is active. README/operator-guide step 4: `hermes-lcm-x` enabled,
  `hermes-lcm` not enabled.

## Rename with a migration path (#471, #472)

- `plugin.yaml` is `name: hermes-lcm-x`; the engine reports `lcm-x`. One module (`plugin_identity.py`)
  owns every produced or compared name.
- The legacy `context.engine: lcm` still selects LCM-X through an alias, with a once-per-process
  `DEPRECATED LCM-X config` warning, an `identity_migration` field in `lcm_status`, and an
  `identity_migration` `warn` check in `lcm_doctor`.
- What cannot be aliased: Hermes matches `plugins.enabled` against the manifest name before any plugin
  code runs. A config that enables only `hermes-lcm` logs `Context engine 'lcm' not found — falling back
  to built-in compressor` and runs without LCM-X; turns handled in that state are not in `lcm.db`.
- Two installed copies cannot both write the store: the second generation logs `Another LCM generation is
  already loaded` and stays inert.
- `scripts/install.sh` installs to `plugins/hermes-lcm-x`, reuses an existing `plugins/hermes-lcm` checkout
  of the same tree, prints the migration steps when it finds a legacy install or config, and never edits
  `config.yaml` or deletes anything.

Migration (one LCM copy; change the config while Hermes is stopped):

1. Stop Hermes; check out this release in the existing clone (`git fetch --tags && git checkout
   v0.24.0`) or a new checkout, then run `scripts/install.sh`. A clone that tracks `main` with
   `git pull --ff-only` gets the current `main`, not necessarily this release.
2. In `plugins.enabled` replace `hermes-lcm` with `hermes-lcm-x`; set `context.engine: lcm-x`.
3. Start Hermes; check that `hermes plugins` lists `hermes-lcm-x` and the log shows `LCM plugin
   loaded — lossless context management active`.

Managed fleets (PCS / managed-plugin payloads) stay pinned to v0.23.x until their own config migration
stages `hermes-lcm-x`.

## Hermes plugin-catalog admission (#473)

- `post_llm_call` registers through `ctx.register_hook` when the host provides it (direct
  `PluginManager._hooks` fallback otherwise). `plugin.yaml` declares `pre_llm_call`, `post_llm_call`,
  `subagent_start` and `subagent_stop`.
- `scripts/update.sh` is removed (catalog rule: no self-updater). Update a branch checkout with
  `git pull --ff-only` + `scripts/install.sh`, a tag checkout with `git fetch --tags && git checkout <tag>`
  + `scripts/install.sh`, and a catalog install with `hermes plugins update hermes-lcm-x`.
- Install-scanner findings neutralized with no behavior change; the README lists every remaining
  informational finding with a reason. No `caution` or `dangerous` findings remain.

## Governance: required AI review check retired (#474, #475)

The required `AI review exact-head` check is retired. Enforcement is strict exact-head CI (six checks),
required review-thread resolution and merge commits only; AI review is recorded evidence plus a `land-pr`
obligation. Maintainer-facing only; no product code.

## Known follow-ups and limitations (tracked)

- #493, #497, #500 — rare paths where the positional ingest cursor can skip a row: an in-process rewrite
  of the already-ingested last row; a Hermes repair that merges assistants one turn after dropping an
  orphan tool row; a re-issued identical call-only row after the host drops the adopted one (native only).
- #496 — other in-place rewrites of the current user row (gateway timestamp, Discord note, CLI
  voice/model-switch notes) are not yet recorded as host rewrites the way #494's trim is.
- #488 — known limitation, unchanged from rc3. A user message that is, or begins with, a byte-exact copy
  of one of the session's own summary blocks can be taken for generated context by a restart
  reconciliation and not stored. A fix is in review; it did not make rc4.
- #499 — a new user turn the host merges into the compacted head can be re-ingested on later restarts.
  With `fresh_tail_count` ≤ 6 in place, compaction can stop publishing, and at 0 the merged turn can be
  lost (the #488 class). Re-measured on rc4: 32/32 cells; publication with tail 0 is 3/3 without a restart and 1/3 across one; tails 1 and 6 are 1/3 in place and 2/3 with rotation; tail 32 is 3/3. Stored-row / duplicate-row ranges by tail 0 / 1 / 6 / 32: 54–148 / 0–86, 67–148 / 10–90, 85–178 / 26–120, 202–332 / 93–216.
- #489 — a crash between a rotation's parent end and child start re-stores the fresh tail (duplicates only).
- #505, #506, #507 — rotation-carry follow-ups from #504, all without loss: the ignore-pattern scan is slow when
  another conversation interleaves writes; with proactive recall on (off by default) the summary carrier is skipped;
  if both proof writes fail, the child's publication cannot see the carry ranges it holds in memory; carrier
  token accounting counts the summary prefix.
- #485 — rows duplicated by pre-fix compaction replays stay in `lcm.db`; a precise detector and a
  mark-as-superseded repair (never delete) are tracked.
- #491 — the `api_key` redaction pattern misses env-style names such as `OPENAI_API_KEY=`.
- #479 — `LCM_NATIVE_RECOVERY=true` aborts every compaction on Hermes v0.21.4 (a host stale-attempt
  check); fixed in Hermes v0.21.5 (`v2026.9.24`). Keep native recovery off (the default) on older hosts.
- Managed fleets: staging `hermes-lcm-x` in fleet configs is a separate fleet-migration change.
- #380 — the privacy-posture flip is not in this release; which train carries it is an owner decision.
- Hermes plugin catalog: the `hermes-lcm-x` entry is submitted after GA, pinned to the GA commit.

## Benchmark boundary

rc3 → rc4 changes ingest bookkeeping only: which rows the compaction commit, restart reconciliation and
rotation publication store or skip, where ingestion resumes, and (with native recovery on) which rows
Hermes' native compressor sees. Context assembly changes in one layout only: with no system message, the
summary is merged into the oldest kept user turn (#495). Recall ranking and the privacy transforms are
unchanged. No benchmark instrument in `bench/` calls `compress()` or context assembly; the only session-hook
caller is the release-gauntlet Phase A instrument (`on_session_start`), which this gauntlet re-runs. The banked
rows keep their commits of record and this train adds no ledger row.

## Upgrade

Follow the migration steps above. No schema change: a `lcm.db` created by v0.23.3 reopens on this tree
with an identical logical dump, row counts and search hits. After use it holds extra metadata rows (the
commit proof per compacted session, carry ranges per rotated session, host-rewrite identities), which
older releases ignore.
Rollback: stop Hermes, check out v0.23.3, restore `plugins.enabled: [hermes-lcm]` and
`context.engine: lcm`. v0.23.3 and rc3 open the same `lcm.db`; they do not read version 3 proofs, so a
restart after rollback reconciles conservatively: no loss, but it can store rows again. Measured in the rc4 gauntlet (Phase B): an rc4 store with two committed compactions, trailing-newline prompts, two `host_rewrite_identity:*` rows and carry ranges rolled back to rc3 and, separately, to v0.23.3 — 0 rows lost, 6 duplicate rows, 65 rows in total and `quick_check=ok` after three old-tree turns in both cases; a plain v0.23.3 → rc4 → v0.23.3 round trip kept all 31 rows with no new doctor problems.
